quarantine.detail: Regenerates docs/reports/atm-2-1-final-closure.md from live data and expects the row "420-cell paired A/B v4 met rollout metrics and safety controller | pass". The current data no longer yields that verdict, consistent with real-paired-ab-analyzer-v3 reading inconclusive. It also rewrites the tracked report, so it needs a fixture data set and a temporary output root.

Snapshots live repository state: it asserts broker replay status stays remain-open "while closure evidence is incomplete". The evidence is now complete, so the command correctly reports ready-to-close and exits 0. The test needs a fixture instead of the live repository.
Runs scripts/analyze-captain-parallel-ledger.ts over the live .atm ledger, so its counts follow current work.

Needs full git history: acc5 depends on whether a recorded SHA is reachable, and the depth-1 CI checkout cannot answer that, so the status is unmet. Passes in a full clone. Enabling it would require fetch-depth: 0 in Product CI.

The test now asserts the map contract rather than frozen totals, but it still cannot pass: scripts/validate-four-plan-closeout-blocker-map.ts reports source digest mismatches for plan-3x-4x-backlog-disposition-census.json, plan-3x-4x-independent-certificate.json and others, so the committed map is stale against its own sources. The repository has no generator for this map, and editing the recorded digests by hand would fabricate a certification, so refreshing it needs an owner decision on who regenerates the map.

Needs full git history: it asserts that origin/main descends from the SHA the certificate is bound to, which a depth-1 CI checkout cannot establish. Enabling it would require fetch-depth: 0 in Product CI.
Reviews the live docs/reports/reviews/plan-3x-4x-objective-authority-review.json, which is regenerated as objectives are certified.

Expects at least one governance residue receipt in the live .atm history; the residue it was written against has since been cleaned, so the census is legitimately empty. It also rewrites docs/reports/historical-governance-residue-cleanup.md, so it needs a fixture history and a temporary output root.

Asserts the CLI owner shard stays at or below 600 physical lines; the file is 1256 lines, so the budget was already exceeded more than twofold before this session added ten mappings (~70 lines) for the extracted team-legacy modules. Splitting the shard is the fix, not relaxing the budget.

Runs scripts/validate-prompt-scoped-next.ts over many routing scenarios. Two real routing defects it exposed are fixed (journaling vs repair intent, 17a27270f). It now stops at the batch scenario: asking for an exact task id inside an active batch reports task-queue-head-claim-blocked instead of ATM_NEXT_TASK_QUEUE_READY, because the prompt carries no actor and the queue head already holds the batch’s own active claim, so diagnoseClaimReadinessForTasks treats it as a blocker. Whether an actor-less query should warn instead of block is an owner decision; do not relax the gate just to make the test pass.
Runs scripts/validate-plan32-terminal-verdict-fail-closed.ts against live data and expects a terminal verdict that the current state no longer produces (verdict not-complete, failClosed false).

Runs scripts/validate-plan4-successor-wave-consumption.ts against live reports; it fails on a source digest mismatch for docs/reports/plan-3x-4x-backlog-disposition-census.json, which is regenerated as the census changes.
Asserts over the live docs/reports/plan4-successor-wave-objective-map.json, which is regenerated as the wave progresses.
Passes, but on Linux leaves packages/cli/dist/atm.mjs modified; on Windows it also failed when run next to other tests.
Passes, but on Linux leaves packages/cli/dist/atm.mjs modified.
Compiles runbook completion evidence from live docs/reports/plan-3x-4x-runbook-completion-evidence.json and the live evidence ledger, so the verdict follows current state.
Reviews release authority from the live docs/reports/plan-3x-4x-runbook-completion-evidence.json, so its verdict follows current state.

Reads the planning repository through resolvePlanningRoot(), which defaults to a sibling 3KLife checkout (override: ATM_PLANNING_REPO_ROOT). A CI clone has no such sibling, so the census denominator is 0. It needs a fixture planning root instead of the live one.

Asserts on live repository state for the historical TASK-MAO-0043: it expects a complete close, but the dashboard reports a partial close because the planning-mirror field cannot be confirmed without the planning repository checked out beside this one. Reporting partial when the mirror is unverifiable is fail-closed and correct; the test needs a fixture instead of the live ledger.

Expects a historical-delivery close to route to the tasks-close backend, but the backend is tasks-close only when the planning-authority delivery gate passes. The fixture supplies a fabricated sha (abc123def456) that cannot verify, so the product fail-closes to tasks-reconcile, which is correct. The fixture needs a real commit that touches the declared deliverables.

Same root cause as taskflow-open-orchestration: host policy allocates the next task id by scanning the profile repository’s docs/tasks, not the --cwd fixture, so the expected TASK-GOVERNED-0002 depends on whether a 0001 card is left in this repository. Whether a profile may redirect reads and writes outside --cwd is an owner decision.

Root-caused 2026-09-20: taskflow open resolves its output root from the profile path (resolveTaskflowOpenOutputRoot returns the profile repo git root), not from --cwd. The test passes a profile that lives in this repository, so the generated card lands in the framework repo docs/tasks instead of the requested cwd, and the run dirties the worktree. Whether a profile may redirect writes outside --cwd is an owner decision; do not change the resolver to make the test pass.
